title: I’m building Kiln, an open-source toolchain that lets AI agents build 3D assets as code. To stress-test it, I made 5 worlds (167 CC0 assets).
author: MattMaxBuilds
selftext:
About a month ago I open-sourced Kiln, a code-driven 3D asset toolchain for AI coding agents. Agents can build everything from procedural primitives to custom geometry, work with materials and textures, render and inspect what they made, and keep refining it until it’s right.

One question I kept getting was whether you could actually build anything substantial with it. One-off models are fun, but I wanted to see how the workflow holds up when you need dozens of assets that have to work together in one place. So I built five environments, with 167 agent-authored assets between them.

The video showcases:

* **Cabin in the Woods (53 assets):** A interactive PSX-style horror scene with a modular, furnished cabin, a forest, spiders, a shotgun and something lurking in the woods.
* **Foundry Floor (62 assets):** An industrial semiconductor fab with machinery, robots, automated transport and plenty of moving parts.
* **Golden Gate Bridge (8 assets):** A large-scale bridge environment you can actually drive across.
* **Shapes & Seasons Farm (23 assets):** A stylized farm with buildings, crops, animals and equipment.
* **Troy (21 assets):** A Bronze Age city with walls, a temple, armies, ships and a battlefield where you can play as Achilles or Hector.

Every asset was written as JavaScript by a coding agent using Kiln’s geometry and material tools. The agent renders its work, inspects the result and revises the source. That loop is a big part of what I’m exploring. I’d rather have an agent iterate on geometry it understands and can edit precisely than get a one-shot mesh I can’t change without starting over.

I directed the builds, reviewed the results, developed the toolchain, and assembled the environments. None of the individual assets were modeled by hand.

All 167 assets are released under CC0, so you can download the GLBs and use them in personal or commercial projects without attribution. The editable Kiln source is included too, so you can bring any asset back into the toolchain and have your own agent modify, extend or completely rework it.

The scenes run in Three.js, which Kiln is also built on, and everything in the video is rendered by the actual scenes, not a separate offline renderer. Some of them are even interactive, though I wouldn’t go calling them full games just yet lol.

Building these worlds turned out to be a really good stress test. Scale consistency, pivots, materials, topology, draw calls and collision all get a lot more interesting when you’re dealing with dozens of models in one environment. A lot of those lessons went straight back into Kiln’s core, QA tooling and agent skills, so the next agent starts from a better place.

There’s still plenty of room to improve. I wouldn’t call these finished production assets, but they’re already useful for prototyping, kitbashing and building out environments. More importantly, the source is there to keep improving them instead of starting over.

I’ve also been moving pretty fast on Kiln itself since the first post. It’s now at v1.2.3, with an npm package, MCP server, CLI and TypeScript SDK. Thanks to everyone who’s tried it out and shared feedback so far!

Longer term, I’d like the asset library to grow into a community-driven collection of reusable 3D content. People creating new models and packs, others remixing existing ones, and hopefully sharing their improvements back. All freely available, and not tied to a particular game engine or workflow.

**Links:**

* GitHub (MIT): [https://github.com/instruktlabs/kiln](https://github.com/instruktlabs/kiln)
* Site, interactive scenes and free CC0 asset packs: [https://kilnstudio.tools](https://kilnstudio.tools)
* Discord: [https://discord.gg/fSWVbMdQXK](https://discord.gg/fSWVbMdQXK)

I also started a Discord for Kiln and the wider community of people working on AI, 3D, games and procedural generation. You don’t have to be using Kiln to join. I’d like it to be a place where people can share their projects, try out different workflows and help push this stuff forward.

If you bring any of these assets or new assets made in Kiln into a real project, I’d love to hear how it goes. Which engine did you use, and what did you have to fix on import: scale, pivots, materials, hierarchy, collision? And if you’ve got ideas for what world or asset pack I should tackle next, I’m all ears.
